cards.art: owl in academic robes holding hourglass
cards.lore: Since 1952, the Sight & Sound cabal of critics summons itself every decade to dictate global taste. 1,639 critics participated in 2022 to remind you that your favorite movie is trash.
cards.name: THE DECENNIAL ORACLE
cards.power: Gatekeeper's Toll – Exhausts 3 opponent attention tokens by forcing them to wait 10 years for a completely arbitrary paradigm shift.

cards.art: octopus director stealing screenplay from screenwriter
cards.lore: Added in 1992, the directors' separate poll proves that filmmakers completely disagree with critics. 480 directors voted in 2022 to elevate their own cinematic kayfabe above journalists.
cards.name: THE DIRECTOR'S CUT
cards.power: Auteur's Hubris – Steals all credit from the writer and crew tokens. Automatically counters any criticism by claiming it's about the process.

cards.art: sheep herd clutching identical movie tickets
cards.lore: Audience polls repeatedly vote for Star Wars or The Godfather. The masses demand the myth they have already purchased.
cards.name: THE HERD CONSENSUS
cards.power: Nostalgia Farm – Extracts infinite financial capital by repeating the same comfortable formula. Destroys all nuance tokens in play.

cards.art: toad in national flag cape behind fortress walls
cards.lore: National polls exist primarily to validate local funding. Every nation has a mathematically proven greatest film that no one outside its borders has ever seen.
cards.name: THE REGIONAL BIAS
cards.power: Echo Chamber – Grants invulnerability to any film produced within the player's own borders. Ignores all international context.

cards.art: husky dog holding a glowing sled ornament
cards.lore: Topped the Sight & Sound poll for five consecutive decades (1962–2002). 46 critics in 2002 maintained the ultimate kayfabe that a movie about a newspaper tycoon is the peak of human art.
cards.name: CITIZEN SLED-DOG
cards.power: Rosebud Extraction – Forces all opponents to spend their turn debating the symbolic meaning of a child's toy. Generates 5 Pretension Points.

cards.art: dizzied pigeon spiraling down a staircase
cards.lore: Dethroned the Kane dog in 2012 when 191 critics decided Alfred Hitchcock's Vertigo—a film literally about obsession and heights—was the new objective truth.
cards.name: SPIRAL PIGEON
cards.power: Obsessive Sabotage – Target player becomes dizzy, replaying the exact same trauma loop 3 turns while dressing up a companion token.

cards.art: exhausted poodle peeling potatoes in fluorescent kitchen
cards.lore: Jeanne Dielman conquered the 2022 Sight & Sound critics' poll, weaponizing three hours of real-time kitchen chores to obliterate capitalist entertainment metrics.
cards.name: POTATO-PEELING POODLE
cards.power: Durational Labor – Forces all opponents to skip 3 hours of real-time gameplay to experience the crushing weight of domestic drudgery.

cards.art: gaunt fox clutching bicycle wheel on cobblestones
cards.lore: Topped the very first Sight & Sound poll in 1952 with a mere 25 more ballots. Neorealism proved that true cinematic power comes from making the audience feel terrible about post-war poverty.
cards.name: BICYCLE-THIEF FOX
cards.power: Neorealist Guilt – Drains all Joy tokens from the board. Opponents must donate half their resources out of pure, unadulterated pity.

cards.art: macaque in tuxedo touching black monolith
cards.lore: 2001: A Space Odyssey topped the 2022 directors poll. Filmmakers united to decree that a slow-moving dialogue-free void is the pinnacle of the moving image.
cards.name: MONOLITH MACAQUE
cards.power: Evolutionary Bore – Upgrades player's intelligence tokens while simultaneously cutting them from everyone else at the table.

cards.art: elderly turtle watching son's back as he leaves
cards.lore: Yasujiro Ozu's Tokyo Story topped the Directors' poll with 48 votes. The ultimate kayfabe that domestic perfection is achieved by placing a camera two feet off the floor and not moving it.
cards.name: TOKYO TURTLE STORY
cards.power: Generational Guilt – Inflicts passive-aggressive emotional damage. Opponents instantly call their parents and apologize for being busy.

cards.art: seven macaques in armor defending terrified village
cards.lore: Seven Samurai (1954) was voted the greatest foreign-language film in a 2018 BBC poll of 209 critics. The foundation myth of every modern action ensemble, extracted from Japanese history.
cards.name: SEVEN MACAQUES
cards.power: Mercenary Labor – Sacrifices your own units to protect a village of ungrateful peasants. Grants mortal legendary status.

cards.art: octopus in director's chair surrounded by blank storyboards
cards.lore: Fellini's 8½ topped the 2015 LodZ poll of 279 Polish film professionals. Directors love nothing more than watching a film about how incredibly hard it is to be a director.
cards.name: 8½ OCTO-AUTEUR
cards.power: Creative Block – You may refuse to take your turn instead, gain points by loudly explaining why your inability to play is actually a masterpiece.

cards.art: pig in antebellum dress against burning sunset
cards.lore: Gone with the Wind was voted the favorite film of Americans in 2008 and 2014 Harris Interactive polls. The ultimate ending myth of the American public, immune to critical re-evaluation.
cards.name: WIND-BLOWN PIG
cards.power: Historical Amnesia – Adjusts the rules of the past to suit the player. Generates massive wealth tokens while ignoring problematic lore.

cards.art: pug in three-piece suit making offer across marble desk
cards.lore: The Godfather was voted #1 by Entertainment Weekly, Time Out, and 10,000 Empire readers. The undisputed heavyweight champion of masculine fantasy projection.
cards.name: MAFIA PUG
cards.power: Offer Refusal – Forces opponent to instantly forfeit their hand, or wake up with their favorite card destroyed.

cards.art: penguin in Vader mask surrounded by merchandise
cards.lore: The Empire Strikes Back was voted the best film of all time by over 250,000 Empire magazine readers. The kayfabe that sequel IP ownership is the highest art form.
cards.name: GALACTIC PENGUIN
cards.power: Merchandising Empire – Extracts real-world currency from opponents every time they feel a shred of childhood nostalgia.

cards.art: hippo in Edwardian dress on sinking deckchair
cards.lore: Titanic was voted the greatest hit of all time by 6,000 Chinese movie fans in a 2008 China Daily poll. A global phenomenon built on the extraction of pure teenage emotional labor.
cards.name: SINKING HIPPO
cards.power: Tear Extraction – Floods the board. Opponents lose 2 turns weeping uncontrollably over entirely avoidable tragedies.

cards.art: chihuahua levitating above bed, head rotating
cards.lore: The Exorcist was voted the best horror film by 150 experts in a 2012 Time Out poll. Weaponized Catholic guilt proven to be the most effective mechanism for cinematic terror.
cards.name: POSSESSED CHIHUAHUA
cards.power: Faith Sabotage – Forces opponents to abandon their most deeply held beliefs. Deals psychological damage that bypasses all shields.

cards.art: barefoot hound running through exploding building
cards.lore: Voted the best action film by Time Out New York and the greatest Christmas movie by Empire readers. The myth that an everyman can defeat European terrorists with no shoes on.
cards.name: HARD-DYING HOUND
cards.power: Holiday Hijack – Permanently reclassifies any opponent's peaceful phase into an explosive combat zone. Yippee-ki-yay.

cards.art: hyena in blonde wig and pearls playing saxophone
cards.lore: Some Like It Hot was voted the best comedy in a poll of 253 global critics by the BBC in 2017. A masterpiece of cross-dressing survival kayfabe.
cards.name: HOT SAXOPHONE HYENA
cards.power: Perfect Imperfection – Nullifies any penalty by declaring Nobody's perfect. Gains immunity to critical logic.

cards.art: woodpecker with elongating beak holding puppet strings
cards.lore: Pinocchio was voted the best animated movie by Time Out in 2014. The animation industry's foundational kayfabe: extracting soul from graphite and ink.
cards.name: WOODEN WOODPECKER
cards.power: Deceptive Whimsy – Tells a lie that looks beautiful. Opponents lose 3 resources believing in whimsy while turning into donkeys.

cards.art: rooster in tailcoat amid collapsing chandelier and fainting guests
cards.lore: Voted the best French film by Time Out Paris and the best European film by Cinemateca Portuguesa. Jean Renoir's ultimate exposé of upper-class societal kayfabe.
cards.name: RULES OF THE GAME ROOSTER
cards.power: Bourgeois Collapse – Causes all high-society tokens to destroy themselves in a misunderstanding over a romantic affair.

cards.art: bat with Nosferatu claw-fingers emerging from burning copyright documents
cards.lore: Tied for best European film in the 1994 Cinemateca Portuguesa. An illegal rip-off of Dracula that survived by sheer, unadulterated visual trauma.
cards.name: NOSFERATU BAT
cards.power: Copyright Infringement – Drains the blood from the original source material. Survives even if a court orders all your cards destroyed.

cards.art: pelican smashing film reels together on battleship deck
cards.lore: Battleship Potemkin topped the 1951 Brussels World's Fair poll. Eisenstein's kayfabe: inventing modern editing just to legitimize a state revolution.
cards.name: POTEMKIN PELICAN
cards.power: Montage Shock – Smashes all unrelated cards together to force a new, highly propagandistic emotional response from the opponent.

cards.art: chameleon with film-camera eye filming a chaotic city street
cards.lore: Man with a Movie Camera topped the 2014 Sight & Sound documentary poll. Dziga Vertov's radical assault on the very concept of fictional acting.
cards.name: CAMERA-EYE CHAMELEON
cards.power: Kino-Eye Truth – Removes all narrative illusions from the board. Forces opponents to look at raw, unscripted mechanical reality.

cards.art: stallion rearing at frontier sunset, erasing map borders
cards.lore: Voted best Western film in 1996 Nickel Odeon poll of experts. John Ford's ultimate construction of the American geographic kayfabe.
cards.name: STAGECOACH STALLION
cards.power: Frontier Manifestation – Pushes opponent tokens out of their territory to establish your own heroic, highly sanitized national origin myth.

cards.art: raccoon in trenchcoat staring at rain-soaked neon city
cards.lore: Blade Runner was voted the best sci-fi film by a panel of 56 scientists in The Guardian (2004). The scientists agreed: corporate dystopian depression is our most likely future.
cards.name: REPLICANT RACCOON
cards.power: Tears in Rain – Your best cards are deleted upon expiration. Opponent must ponder what it means to be truly alive.

cards.art: two bovines on opposite sides of mountain, not looking at each other
cards.lore: Brokeback Mountain topped the 2016 Time Out London poll for LGBT+ cinema. A masterclass in weaponizing the mythic masculine western against itself.
cards.name: BROKEBACK BOVINE
cards.power: Unspoken Anguish – Prevents players from taking direct action. All combat must be resolved through repressed longing and societal slumber.

cards.art: seagull with outstretched wings in prison yard rain
cards.lore: Voted the greatest film by Empire readers in 2006. The ultimate cinematic kayfabe: patience and a rock hammer will conquer all systemic injustice.
cards.name: SHAWSHANK SEAGULL
cards.power: Basic Cable Immortality – Even if defeated, this card returns to the board every single Sunday afternoon, consistently unavoidable.

cards.art: tiger cub watching rainstorm through bamboo fence
cards.lore: Topped the British Film Institute's user poll of Top 10 Indian Films in 2002. Satyajit Ray's masterpiece that forced the West to admit cinema existed outside their bubble.
cards.name: PATHER PANCHALI TIGER
cards.power: Humanist Revelation – Forces the opponent to stop playing the game and simply appreciate the tragic beauty of ordinary life.

cards.art: panda on crumbling wall watching spring blossoms fall
cards.lore: Spring in a Small Town (1948) was ranked #1 by the Hong Kong Film Awards Association in 2005. A subtle, poetic sabotage of grand, noisy historical narratives.
cards.name: SPRING TOWN PANDA
cards.power: Post-war Paralysis – Locks down the board. No player may attack; they can only sigh deeply and reflect on broken marriages.

cards.art: cat in maid uniform stirring something into wealthy family's teapot
cards.lore: The Housemaid (1960) topped a 2024 poll of 240 critics by the Korean Film Archive. The blueprint for Korean cinema's obsession with violent class warfare.
cards.name: HOUSEMAID CAT
cards.power: Domestic Subversion – Infiltrates the opponent's resource deck and slowly poisons it from the inside while cleaning their house.

cards.art: dragon in trenchcoat diving in slow-motion amid falling doves
cards.lore: A Better Tomorrow (1986) was voted the second-best Chinese film ever. John Woo established the kayfabe that true brotherhood requires shooting 500 people in slow-mo.
cards.name: HONG KONG ACTION DRAGON
cards.power: Heroic Bloodshed – Generates infinite ammo tokens. Allows you to die in slow motion, guaranteeing you win the moral vote.

cards.art: iguana in linen suit watching revolution from balcony
cards.lore: Memories of Underdevelopment was voted best Latin American film by dn critics in 1999. Tomás Gutiérrez Alea's documentation of the ultimate revolutionary spectator sport.
cards.name: UNDERDEVELOPMENT IGUANA
cards.power: Bourgeois Alienation – Allows the player to observe the game losing without ever taking responsibility for anything.

cards.art: armadillo flipping roulette table in crumbling favela alley
cards.lore: The Red Light Bandit (1968) was voted the best Brazilian film in a 2011 Filco 3 lista poll. A harsh, nihilistic middle finger to polished cinema aesthetics.
cards.name: RED LIGHT ARMADILLO
cards.power: Marginal Cinema – Flips the game rules upside down. Trash tokens become gold tokens; logic becomes an affront.

cards.art: llama in chains turning toward camera as overseer falls
cards.lore: Prisioneros de la tierra (1939) was repeatedly voted the greatest Argentine film by the Museo del Cine. A raw, blazing spotlight exposing the extraction of indigenous labor.
cards.name: PRISONER LLAMA
cards.power: Exploitation Backlash – When your health reaches zero, instantly destroy the opponent's most expensive, capital-generating unit.

cards.art: vulture in revolutionary bandolier stripping hero medals off cards
cards.lore: Vámonos con Pancho Villa (1936) was voted the best Mexican film in a 1994 Somos 500 poll. It systematically dismantles the romantic kayfabe of revolutionary war.
cards.name: PANCHO VILLA VULTURE
cards.power: Disillusionment – Strips all Hero tags from opponent's cards. Everyone is revealed to be a flawed, violent opportunist.

cards.art: kangaroo vanishing into red rock formation leaving only picnic basket
cards.lore: Picnic at Hanging Rock was voted the best Australian film in a 1996 poll. The ultimate kayfabe of the Australian Gothic: that the continent simply eats people.
cards.name: HANGING ROCK KANGAROO
cards.power: Unsolved Mystery – Leaves the game abruptly. The opponent spends the rest of the match trying to figure out what just happened.

cards.art: wombat warrior mid-punch, both fists bleeding
cards.lore: Once Were Warriors was voted the best New Zealand film by a 2014 Fairfax Media poll. A brutal shattering of the picturesque, hobbit-filled New Zealand tourism myth.
cards.name: ONCE WERE WOMBATS
cards.power: Generational Trauma – Deals heavy damage, but inflicts an equal amount of psychological recoil damage to your own deck.

cards.art: bulldog in trench coat emerging from sewer holding watered-down medicine bottles
cards.lore: Voted the best British film ever in a 1999 BFI poll. Orson Welles stealing a movie with five minutes of screen time and a monologue about the Swiss.
cards.name: THIRD MAN BULLDOG
cards.power: Cuckoo Clock Economics – Steals opponent's health potions and dilutes them, profiting off the post-war black market.

cards.art: armored parrot with severed wing still squawking at opponent
cards.lore: Monty Python and the Holy Grail was voted the best British picture by 7,000 film fans (2004). The absolute pinnacle of unhinged, budget-less cinematic sabotage.
cards.name: HOLY GRAIL PARROT
cards.power: Flesh Wound – Refuses to be removed from the board when even completely destroyed. Continues to shout abuse at the opponent.

cards.art: lynx weaving incomprehensible tapestry around confused opponent
cards.lore: Voted the best Czech film of all time by journalists in 1994 and 1998. The grand kayfabe that medieval brutality is best depicted through avant-garde poetry.
cards.name: MARKETA LAZAROVA LYNX
cards.power: Pagan Attrition – Confuses the opponent with three hours of non-linear, experimental narrative until they forfeit out of exhaustion.

cards.art: boar in grey suit stamping mountains of identical forms
cards.lore: Teddy Bear (1981) was voted the best movie in Poland by 49 experts at 2013 Filmfest PL. Pure satirical venom aimed directly at the daily kayfabe of Communist absurdism.
cards.name: TEDDY BEAR BOAR
cards.power: Bureaucratic Sabotage – Opponent must fill out a form in triplicate before drawing a card. Failure results in immediate arrest.

cards.art: wolf herding figures in circles on shrinking landscape
cards.lore: Voted the best Hungarian film in a 2000 critics' poll. Miklós Jancsó's masterclass in how to extract power through sheer, geometric intimidation.
cards.name: ROUND-UP WOLF
cards.power: Psychological Enclosure – Reduces the board size every turn until the opponent has absolutely nowhere to move.

cards.art: wide-eyed bear emerging from burning village, ash-faced
cards.lore: Come and See was voted the best Belarusian film by 49 experts in 2024. The total, uncompromised destruction of the glorious war movie kayfabe.
cards.name: COME AND SEE BEAR
cards.power: Deafening Roar – Mutes all sound in the game. Deals permanent psychic damage to whoever looks at the card too long.

cards.art: deer mid-collapse, body igniting into revolutionary flames
cards.lore: The Deer (1974) was voted the best Iranian film in a 2009 poll of 92 critics. A fierce social critique that accidentally predicted and fueled an actual real-world revolution.
cards.name: IRANIAN DEER
cards.power: Tragic Rebellion – When destroyed, ignites a cultural revolution token that permanently changes the meta of the game.

cards.art: camel smuggling ancient artifacts past tomb entrance at night
cards.lore: The Night of Counting the Years (1969) was voted the best Arab film by 44 film professionals. The mythic clash between surviving the present and honoring the ancient dead.
cards.name: NIGHT COUNTING CAMEL
cards.power: Heritage Theft – Steals artifacts from the opponent's graveyard to sell for immediate, short-term survival points.

cards.art: sloth in oversized uniform hiding behind tiny bush from sergeant
cards.lore: Giv'at Halfon Eina Ona was voted Favorite Israeli Film by 25,000 web users. An absurdist deconstruction of the hyper-militarized national kayfabe.
cards.name: HALFON HILL SLOTH
cards.power: Draft Evasion – Ignores all combat phases. Gains points purely through comedic incompetence and avoiding authority.

cards.art: tortoise standing on dam, watching cracked fields
cards.lore: Dry Summer (1963) was voted the best Turkish film released between 1923-2013. A neo-realist exposé showing that controlling the water means controlling the myth.
cards.name: DRY SUMMER TORTOISE
cards.power: Resource Monopoly – Controls the water supply. Opponents must pay a heavy toll to un-tap any of their cards.

cards.art: skeletal reindeer driving ghost carriage through New Year's Eve snow
cards.lore: The Phantom Carriage (1921) was rated the best Swedish film by FLM magazine. Extracting morality from the audience by threatening them with the Grim Reaper's Uber service.
cards.name: PHANTOM CARRIAGE REINDEER
cards.power: New Year's Penance – If played on the last turn, forces the opponent to review every mistake they made in the game and take guilt damage.

cards.art: moose in soldier coat standing in blizzard, completely alone, not moving
cards.lore: The Unknown Soldier (1955) was voted the best Finnish movie by Helsingin Sanomat. The national kayfabe of surviving impossible odds through sheer, miserable grit.
cards.name: UNKNOWN MOOSE
cards.power: Sisu Endurance – Refuses to die when HP hits zero. Survives purely out of stubborn, frozen spite.

cards.art: puffin dissolving into volcanic tundra
cards.lore: Children of Nature (1991) was voted the best Icelandic film. A rejection of western desire dying in favor of merging with the mythological landscape.
cards.name: NATURE PUFFIN
cards.power: Pagan Return – Escapes the board's rules entirely to return to the earth deck. Cannot be targeted by modern corporate mechanics.

cards.art: walrus detonating own car while trying to light cigarette
cards.lore: Blinkende lygte was voted best Danish movie to the YouGov public poll. The ultimate proof that true bringers are actually functioning, loveable, dysfunctional sociopaths.
cards.name: FLICKERING WALRUS
cards.power: Criminal Incompetence – Attempting to attack usually results in the player accidentally blowing up their own resources, to the audience's delight.

cards.art: badger stuffing ballot box in Sight & Sound polling booth
cards.lore: Wikipedia warns: Voting systems suffer from surveys that suffer from biases such as self-selection or skewed demographics, while others may be susceptible to interference. SEE?? BIAS!!
cards.name: THE BALLOT BOX BADGER
cards.power: Vote Stacking – Automatically wins any tie-breaker by utilizing skewed demographics and self-selection bias.

cards.art: rat frantically rewriting history book at candlelit desk
cards.lore: What was brilliant in 1952 is boring in 2022. The poll is a record of objective cinematic quality; it is a mirror reflecting the insecurities of the electorate. THEY'RE STEALING THE PAST!!
cards.name: THE RETROSPECTIVE RAT
cards.power: Revisionist History – Changes the stats of a card played 10 turns ago because the current cultural media demands it.

cards.art: pigeon in tuxedo blocking sci-fi and horror cards from entering awards stage
cards.lore: Science fiction, horror, and comedy get their own lists because the serious decennial critics refuse to let aliens, ghosts, or laughter sit at the adult table. THE ELITES.
cards.name: THE GENRE PIGEONHOLE
cards.power: Categorical Dismissal – Prevents any Genre card from ever winning the Overall Best title, trapping them forever in their own specialized echo chamber.

cards.art: weasel in glasses pointing at seventeen-tab browser window
cards.lore: List of films voted the best Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia. The ultimate motion picture kayfabe—compiling 100 years of global subjective art into a definitive, bloodless spreadsheet.
cards.name: THE WIKIPEDIA WEASEL
cards.power: Citation Needed – Nullifies any argument at the table by linking to an aggregate of anonymous opinions disguised as objective data.
